author: Adelaar, K. Alexander
title: Where does Malay come from? Twenty years of discussions about homeland, migrations and classifications
notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (JSTOR PDF in Downloads). Reviews the theories of the Malay homeland (§§2-5: West Borneo, between the Kapuas, Batang Lupar and Saribas rivers, p. 13ff.), the external classification of Malayic (§6: Adelaar's 1992a list of Proto-Malayic innovations, p. 12; Malayo-Chamic; Malayo-Sumbawan, Figure 1, p. 13) and its internal classification (§7: Collins's single Bornean Malay subgroup, Nothofer's western Bornean subgroups and his 'Southwest Malay', with Jakarta and Bangka Malay, pp. 14-23). Adelaar finds no diagnostic for a separate Iban branch and treats the western Bornean Malayic-Dayak isolects (Kendayan/Salako, Ibanic) as possible subgroups without entering a tree.
